en_summary: (Reposted by @carlquintanilla) @farrmacro: if new unsecured AI debt prices at 15%, capital won't fund these firms again, so cash burning companies must use equity to fund 2 to 3 more years of losses. $CRWV
ko_summary: (Reposted by @carlquintanilla) @farrmacro: 새 AI 무담보 부채가 15%에 발행된다면 자본이 다시 이들을 지원하지 않는다는 뜻이며 현금을 태우는 기업은 2~3년 손실을 지분으로 메워야 한다. $CRWV
text:
Matt discusses the current situation but I think It’s really about going forward.  If new unsecured debt in the AI space is being priced at 15%, that’s basically saying capital isn’t going to fund these companies again.  So the companies that are bleeding cash will have to use equity to finance 2-3 more years of operating losses and severely dilute current shareholders.  Yes the projects and chips may survive but that may end up being owned by the securitized debt holders and equity may get wrecked in the process.   Now on top of that you’re seeing secured debt getting priced at 10% now too (see FT article).  Add on some delays, political pushback, permitting issues, and investor concerns about risks and you can run into a situation where private equity doesn’t get paid back anytime soon.  So it’s not “panic”, it’s repricing.  And the reprice may not be so great.   This benefits the companies that are financing a lot of their capex via legacy free cash flow.  The debt heavy new incumbents may have problems.

The Gulf Oil Paradox: Restoring Crude Is Not Restoring Fuel

@robin_j_brooks is right to highlight the IRGC's impact on freight, but the bigger story is market fragmentation. Gulf crude flows have recovered to 91% of pre-war levels; refined-product exports remain below 50% (IEA). Freight has hit $34/bbl and Hormuz war-risk premiums 6–9% of hull value. text:
It is rather remarkable that nearly everything in investing revolves around nominal returns.

Institutional investors determine their strategic asset allocation largely on the basis of nominal data.

Following one of the worst bond bear markets on record, you now have to go back 30 years to find a positive cumulative real return on bonds.

Many investors simply do not realize that three decades of real returns from bond investing have effectively been wiped out.

That does not mean bonds cannot perform well from here, especially now that real yields have turned positive again.

But if you were to use real returns in a standard mean-variance optimization model, as most institutional investors do, there is virtually no chance that bonds would receive an allocation anywhere near 40% in the strategic asset mix.

In fact, bonds receive no allocation at all once you expand the investment universe beyond different types of stocks and bonds.

And the outlook for bonds, something that is almost never incorporated into traditional mean-variance optimization models, becomes significantly less attractive when you factor in the prospect of higher inflation.

en_summary: Warns that the Roadster unveil would be met with indifference by $TSLA investors ($TSLA -3.1% vs NDX -2.3%). Expected financial impact only +$.06/share incremental eps in 2029 (+1.1% of consensus 2029 adj eps of $5.40). Halo effect limited as few care about 0-60 under 1s or flying. TSLA always sells on the news. Remains cautious on $TSLA due to extended valuation, expected negative revisions, and view that unsupervised autonomy becomes commoditized.
ko_summary: Roadster 공개가 $TSLA 투자자들에게 무관심으로 받아들여질 것이라고 경고한다 ($TSLA -3.1% vs NDX -2.3%). 예상 재무 영향은 2029년 주당 증분 EPS +0.06달러(합의 2029년 조정 EPS 5.40달러의 +1.1%). 후광 효과는 제한적이며 0-60 1초 미만이나 비행에 관심 있는 사람이 적다. TSLA는 항상 뉴스 후 매도한다. 확장된 밸류에이션, 예상 부정 수정, 비지도 자율주행이 상품화될 것이라는 견해로 $TSLA에 신중하다.
text: I warned everyone that the Roadster unveil would be met with indifference by TSLA investors  ($TSLA -3.1% vs NDX -2.3%). One, while the engineering and tech were dazzling, the expected financial impact (we estimate +$.06/share incremental eps in 2029) is only +1.1% of consensus 2029 adj eps of $5.40. Second, the halo effect on the $TSLA franchise is likely to be limited since only a tiny subset of U.S. drivers care about going from 0-60 in under 1 second, or that the vehicle can fly short distances while doing flips mid-air.  Third, TSLA always sells on the news after its events and the same principle applies today.  We remain cautious on $TSLA due to its extended valuation, continued expected negative revisions, and our view that unsupervised autonomy becomes commoditized.

zh_summary: @deepakshenoy建議印度央行從其660噸黃金中出售予黃金ETF並存於其金庫，贖回時再買回；這樣更便宜，並可減少黃金進口帶來的外匯需求。
en_summary: @deepakshenoy suggests the RBI sell gold from its 660 tons to Indian gold ETFs and keep it in its vaults, buying back on redemptions; this would be cheaper and reduce FX demand from gold imports.
ko_summary: @deepakshenoy는 인도중앙은행이 보유 금 660톤 중 일부를 금 ETF에 팔아 금고에 보관하고 환매 시 되사자고 제안했다. 더 저렴하고 금 수입에 따른 외환 수요를 줄인다.
text:
Interesting proposal. I believe it will help if rbi effectively sells gold to the etfs and sequesters them in its vaults. So if rbi have 660 tons of gold and etfs want 10 tons, rbi can sell it to them and mark it as such in the rbi vault. 

It will be cheaper and then rbi can always purchase the gold back when there is a redemption. This will also reduce total money in the system since rbi sells and takes out money from the system. 

Eventually it still has custody of the gold, doesn't have to worry about losing access to gold (it can always buy it back) and etf demand is totally fulfilled and safe. 

It will hurt gold vaults to some extent cos we will trust rbi vaults far more than private ones. It will reduce some physical import demand perhaps as etfs own about 120 tons of gold this far but it's growing. Rbi has 660.

My suggestion was that rbi sells gold to jewellers but this does something equivalent and probably better.
